courses.title: Technical Communication
courses.description: Written and oral communication in business correspondence, engineering design methods, report preparation and oral presentations of technical material. Restricted to students in second year of the Manufacturing Engineering Program. [3-0-0]. Prerequisite: One of APSC 176, ENGL 110, ENGL 111, ENGL 112, ENGL 120, ENGL 121, WRDS 150. Equivalency: APSC 201. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: One of APSC 176, ENGL 110, ENGL 111, ENGL 112, ENGL 120, ENGL 121, WRDS 150

courses.title: Introduction to Manufacturing Engineering
courses.description: Core professional and technical skills for manufacturing engineers. Project management, teamwork, design principles, and foundational knowledge in mechanical, materials, electrical, and programming domains through collaborative, hands-on projects. [2-2-0] This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.description: Thermodynamic system and properties, thermodynamic processes; work and heat interactions. Conservation of energy and First Law, internal energy and enthalpy, the Second Law and entropy, application to manufacturing processes. [3-0-1] Prerequisite: All of MATH 101, MATH 152, PHYS 157. Corequisite: MATH 255. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Machine Dynamics
courses.description: Classifications of mechanisms, velocity, acceleration and force analysis, graphical and computer-oriented vector and matrix methods, balancing, flywheels, gears, gear trains, cams. [3-0-2*] Prerequisite: All of MATH 101, MATH 152, PHYS 170. Corequisite: MATH 255. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Production Systems Management I
courses.description: Impact of operations in increasing productivity and reducing waste. [3-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Manufacturing Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Theory, operational constraints, and problem solving in traditional manufacturing processes. Casting, heat treatment, bulk deformation (i.e. rolling, extrusion, drawing), machining, joining, and composites processing. Experiments in process and product characterization. Credit will be granted for only one of MANU 280 or MANU 230. [1-2-0; 1-2-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Manufacturing Engineering Project I
courses.description: Project-based, multi-step manufacturing engineering design and problem solving. [1-4-0; 1-4-0]. Prerequisite: MANU 230. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Production Systems Management II
courses.description: Functional area of production and operations management. Decision-making, capacity planning, aggregate planning, inventory management, distribution planning, materials requirements planning and quality control. [3-0-0]. Prerequisite: MANU 270. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Engineering Materials II
courses.description: Materials selection for different design criteria; importance of shape and processing variables; computer software in selection. Credit will be granted for only one of MTRL 280 or MANU 378. [2-0-3]. Prerequisite: APSC 278. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Manufacturing Processes I
courses.description: Correlation between material properties and processibility for practical engineering manufacturing routes. Calculations and design. Application of heat/mass/fluid transport, mechanics and thermodynamics to manufacturing processes. [2-0-3] Prerequisite: All of APSC 278, APSC 279, MTRL 264, MECH 260 and one of MECH 280, MTRL 263. Corequisite: MANU 261. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: All of APSC 278, APSC 279, MTRL 264, MECH 260 and one of MECH 280, MTRL 263

courses.title: Industrial Automation
courses.description: Principle components of manufacturing automation, modelling of sensors-actuators and control systems, robotic programming, programmable logical control (PLC) systems and development of PLC ladder diagrams. [2-3*-1]. Prerequisite: All of MANU 265, MATH 255. Corequisite: MANU 330. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Special Topics in Manufacturing Engineering
courses.description: Prerequisite: Third-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Topics in Manufacturing Engineering
courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Manufacturing Design Capstone Project
courses.description: Project-based, multi-step, multi-part Capstone design project involving manufacturing engineering design methods, problem solving. [1-4-0; 1-4-0]. Prerequisite: MANU 330. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Biomedical Manufacturing
courses.description: Bulk and nanoscale manufacturing processes for biomedical devices, materials and therapeutics; drug delivery; host-tissue biomaterial interactions; surface modification of medical devices; sterilization techniques; good manufacturing processes; medical device regulation. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Additive Manufacturing Design
courses.description: Design tools and methods for additive manufacturing, complex digital geometry creation, computer aided design tools, additive manufacturing workflow development, producibility analysis, analysis of 3D data sets for suitability to additive manufacturing processes. [2-2-0]. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or greater. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Factory Planning
courses.description: Resources planning, layout and logistics. Modular production and cyber-physical manufacturing systems in laboratory scale, virtual manufacturing and factory automation. [2-2-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Manufacturing Information Systems
courses.description: Data engineering and industrial IoT for smart manufacturing. Implementation of data pipelines, edge/cloud systems, and analytics to integrate factory operations with enterprise platforms. [2-2-0] Prerequisite: MANU 386. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Smart Manufacturing
courses.description: Introduction to smart manufacturing systems and digital transformation strategies. Industry 4.0/5.0, IIoT architectures, smart factories, digital twins, cyber-physical systems, and cybersecurity. [3-2*-0] Prerequisite: All of MANU 330, MANU 386. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Manufacturing for Clean Energy
courses.description: Manufacturing and the net-zero energy transition; renewable, low-carbon and sustainable energy and electricity generation; energy, electricity transport, storage and batteries; hydrogen economy; carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS). [3-0-0]. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or greater. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: AI and Machine Learning Applications in Manufacturing
courses.description: Artificial intelligence, machine learning techniques, Deep learning, Python libraries for machine learning, Basic signal processing techniques, Data Acquisition, Applications in Manufacturing, Use of sound to evaluate operation of CNC machinery, Use of AE sensor to evaluate metal 3D printing. [3-0-1]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Manufacturing Processes II
courses.description: Numerical modelling of manufacturing processes, linkage between material, process, properties and product geometry, heat/mass transport, thermodynamics and design principles applied to practical engineering processes. [2-0-3] Prerequisite: MANU 380. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Manufacturing Processes III
courses.description: Integrating concepts of primary (casting), secondary (deformation), and tertiary (machining and surface treatment) processes and economic and environmental assessment. [2-0-3]. Prerequisite: MANU 380. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Metal Cutting and Machine Tool Vibrations
courses.description: Metal cutting and grinding mechanics; prediction of force-torque-power in turning, drilling, milling and grinding operations. Machine tool vibrations, forced and self-excited vibrations in machining, experimental modal testing of machine tools, chatter, and stability. Credit will be granted for only one of MANU 485 or MECH 592. [3-1*-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Machine and Part Metrology
courses.description: Laser interferometer measurement of volumetric accuracy; error mapping, modelling and compensation of errors, rotation metrology, spindle accuracy. Part dimension and surface metrology. Metrology instruments: coordinate measurement machine, surface profile meter, laser interferometer and ball bar. [2-2-0]. Prerequisite: All of MANU 265, MATH 255, MECH 368. Corequisite: MANU 430. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Special Topics in Manufacturing Engineering
courses.description: [2-2-0]. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
